The circles $r=1$ and $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ intersect at points $A$ and $B,$ as shown above. What are the polar coordinates of the point $B?$
question.worked_solution:
To determine the polar coordinates of the intersection points, we will solve the following system of equations for $r$ and $\theta :$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ r=1\end{aligned}
$$

We begin by setting the equations equal to each other and solving for $\theta .$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation in the interval $[{0}^{∘},\text{ }\,{360}^{∘}),$ we obtain ${\theta }_{1}={60}^{∘}$ and ${\theta }_{2}={300}^{∘}.$  

Also, notice that $r=1$ at both intersection points.

Therefore, polar coordinates of the point $B$ are 

$\,$ $(r,\theta )=(1,{300}^{∘}).$
